solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, number freed: 22 down to 23); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Satirist commentator finally stop legal document

indicators.note: to stop something is to plug it, so one piece sits inside the other like a stopper

parts.note: a wit is a clever, mocking humorist

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word it follows

parts.note: its closing letter

explanation.surface: Someone wants a court order to silence a satirical pundit.
explanation.walkthrough: The final letter of commentator plugs the satirist, sitting between the second and third letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A writ is a formal written order issued by a court, a classic legal document.

clue.text: Shed's at the very least four or five unopened rubbish bags

indicators.note: something left unopened has lost its front, so the first letter goes
to bag something is to capture it, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: rubbish is refuse; without its opening letter it loses the R

indicators.note: the very least of a word is its smallest starting part, here the initial both words share

parts.note: both numbers begin with the same letter, so either way the first letter is the same

explanation.surface: A garden shed holds at least four or five unopened bin bags of rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay. F slips in after the first two letters of the shortened rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: To effuse is to pour out or give off, as a liquid, light or smell is shed.

clue.text: NZ lothario crashing pubs where swingers can hang out?

indicators.note: a lothario crashing about is in wild disorder, so his letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder, taken as written
bars are pubs

explanation.surface: A New Zealand womaniser gatecrashes pubs where sexually liberated swingers gather.
explanation.walkthrough: The swingers of the surface are partner-swappers; in the definition they are gymnasts swinging from apparatus.
explanation.definitionFit: Horizontal bars are the gymnastics apparatus on which gymnasts swing and hang during their routines.

clue.text: Melodies that identify suite aren't sung in performance

indicators.note: a piece in performance is being played out, freely interpreted, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A musical suite in concert has identifying melodies that are played rather than sung.
explanation.definitionFit: Signature tunes are theme melodies that announce and identify a programme or performer.

clue.text: Clears Factor 50, say, when cycling

indicators.note: cycling sends letters round in a loop, so the first letter moves to the back

parts.note: factor 50 is a strong sun cream, an example of sunblock

explanation.surface: Factor 50 sun cream clears your skin of danger while you are out cycling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks Factor 50 as an example of the word wanted; its first letter moves to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To unblock something is to free it of obstruction, so a drain that unblocks clears.

clue.text: Extremely wide mahogany shelves carry delivered Kircaldy pottery

indicators.note: extremely here means at the extremes, taking the first and last letter of each of the next three words

parts.note: its two end letters
its two end letters
its two end letters

indicators.note: a speech is delivered out loud, so the word before is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: to wear clothes is to carry them on the body; spoken, it matches a word for goods

explanation.surface: Wide mahogany shelves hold pottery sent from the Scottish town of Kirkcaldy.
explanation.walkthrough: Wemyss Ware is decorated pottery made in Kirkcaldy, Fife, in Scotland; Wemyss is said 'weems'. The clue spells the town Kircaldy.
explanation.definitionFit: Wemyss Ware was hand-painted pottery produced at the Fife Pottery in Kirkcaldy from the 1880s.

clue.text: Wainwright for one's back down before you and me

indicators.note: back tells us the following word is read from its end to its start

parts.note: down is soft fine hair, fur
you and me together are us

explanation.surface: Wainwright, the fellwalker, gets his back down ahead of the rest of us.
explanation.walkthrough: Rufus Wainwright is a Canadian-American singer-songwriter; the surface suggests Alfred Wainwright, writer of Lake District walking guides.
explanation.definitionFit: Rufus Wainwright is a singer-songwriter, so he is one example of a person with that first name.

clue.text: Good man working in sales picked up Rob, an ever-shining example?

indicators.note: working suggests something busy and being reshaped, so the words after it are reordered

parts.note: ST is short for saint, the crossword's good man
anagram fodder

indicators.note: a word picked up is caught by ear, so we want what sounds like it

parts.note: to rob is to steal

explanation.surface: A decent man in a sales job is overheard being accused of robbery.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: a metal that never tarnishes keeps on shining, so it is an example of something ever-shining.
explanation.definitionFit: Stainless steel is a chromium alloy that resists rust and tarnish, so it stays bright and gleaming.

clue.text: Dutifulness and honour linked to group of spectators repeatedly denied opening

indicators.note: denied its opening twice over means the front letter is removed, then the new front letter too

parts.note: the OBE is a British honour, the Order of the British Empire
an audience is a group of spectators; losing two front letters leaves the rest

explanation.surface: Duty is honoured, but the audience keeps being refused entry.
explanation.walkthrough: AUDIENCE loses A, then U, before joining the honour.
explanation.definitionFit: Obedience is the quality of doing as one is told, closely allied to dutifulness.

clue.text: Social unit that could be kind?

definitions.text: Social unit that could be kind?

parts.note: surface reading: a group of relatives beyond parents and children
setter's reading: a word for relatives, given one more letter, becomes the word kind

explanation.walkthrough: Kin means family; extend it by one letter and you have kind, which also means a family or sort.
explanation.definitionFit: Grandparents, aunts, uncles and cousins together form the wider household network sociologists call this social unit.

clue.text: Tense half of weekend in the thick of endless disaster

indicators.note: endless means the final letter of the phrase before it is cut off

parts.note: T is the grammar abbreviation for tense
the weekend is Saturday and Sunday; one half is the Sunday abbreviation
in the thick of means amid, here without its last letter

explanation.surface: Things get tense halfway through a weekend amid an unending catastrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsunami is a huge sea wave, often caused by an earthquake, that brings natural catastrophe to coasts.

clue.text: Initially take on supporter with reference to sound character?

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: its first letter
taken as written
an ally is a supporter

explanation.surface: Someone takes on a supporter who seems to have a sound, reliable character.
explanation.walkthrough: Sound character suggests good moral fibre; the definition means the quality of a sound, its tone.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonally means in terms of tone, and tone is the character or quality of a musical sound.

clue.text: Olive perhaps 'introduces' chiefly lustful novice

indicators.note: chiefly means mostly, so the word after keeps all but its final letter

parts.note: olive is one shade of green
lustful is horny, here with its final letter dropped

explanation.surface: A girl named Olive leads an innocent beginner into lust.
explanation.walkthrough: Olive looks like a name; it is a colour. The quoted 'introduces' just puts the colour first.
explanation.definitionFit: A greenhorn is an inexperienced newcomer, someone new and untrained in a job or place.

clue.text: In outburst, English, India and China make uninformed assessment

indicators.note: in places the next item inside the word for outburst

parts.note: a gust is a sudden outburst, of wind or feeling
E is the abbreviation for English
India is I in the radio alphabet
china means mate, from rhyming slang 'china plate'

explanation.surface: Amid an angry outburst, England, India and China produce an ill-informed estimate.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney rhyming slang: china plate rhymes with mate, so china means friend.
explanation.definitionFit: To guesstimate is to estimate by guesswork, judging something without the facts to hand.

clue.text: Beats parasites

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the regular sounds of a clock, or moments

explanation.walkthrough: Beats reads as a verb, defeats; it is the noun, like the beats of a clock.
explanation.definitionFit: A clock's ticks are its regular beats, and ticks are also small parasitic arachnids that feed on blood.

clue.text: Most anxious journalist at last accessing bombed site

parts.note: ED is short for editor, the crossword's usual journalist

indicators.note: a bombed building is blown apart, so the letters are scattered and rebuilt
at last points to the final letter of the word that follows

parts.note: its last letter
anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A reporter gets access to a bomb site and is extremely nervous.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgy means tense and nervous, so the edgiest person is the most anxious one.

clue.text: New deal in sport that will always be beaten

indicators.note: in places the reworked word inside the sport
new suggests a fresh version, so the letters of the next word are remade

parts.note: anagram fodder
golf is a sport

explanation.surface: A new sponsorship deal in a sport that is forever losing.
explanation.walkthrough: Beaten here means hammered thin: gold leaf is gold beaten into very fine sheets.
explanation.definitionFit: Gold leaf is made by goldbeaters hammering gold into extremely thin sheets for gilding.

clue.text: Eg UK and Iran are in it somehow, as are their leaders

definitions.text: Eg UK and Iran are in it somehow, as are their leaders

indicators.note: somehow says the letters come together in some unstated arrangement

parts.note: anagram fodder
anagram fodder

indicators.note: leaders are the front letters of the two countries just named

parts.note: its first letter
its first letter

explanation.surface: Britain and Iran both lie in some continent, and so do their heads of state.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the definition and the wordplay: the fodder is are, as, and the leading letters of the two countries.
explanation.definitionFit: Eurasia is the combined landmass of Europe and Asia, containing both Britain and Iran.

clue.text: Extended discussions left head of KGB in tears, on and off

indicators.note: in places the pieces before it inside the shortened word after it
head of points to the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: its first, third and fifth letters

indicators.note: on and off means taking one letter, skipping one, and so on

parts.note: its first letter
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: After long negotiations, a KGB chief walks out in tears, now and again.
explanation.definitionFit: Talks are formal discussions, often prolonged negotiations between parties trying to reach agreement.

clue.text: Actuarial data obliged by law to include conclusions of brief balance sheet

indicators.note: to include something is to take it inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: liable means legally bound

indicators.note: conclusions are the ends, so each following word gives its last letter

parts.note: the last letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: Insurers' statistics must by law include the closing figures of a short balance sheet.
explanation.walkthrough: The three last letters go in after the second letter of the word for legally bound.
explanation.definitionFit: A life table lists mortality rates by age, the core statistical tool actuaries use to price life insurance.

clue.text: Cook Islands checked by British attaché on vacation

parts.note: BR is the abbreviation for British

indicators.note: something checked by another is held in or hemmed by it, so it goes inside
on vacation means emptied out, so only the outer letters remain

parts.note: its two outer letters
IS is the abbreviation for Islands

explanation.surface: A British diplomatic attaché on holiday visits the Cook Islands in the Pacific.
explanation.walkthrough: Cook Islands looks like a place name; Cook alone is the definition, a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To braise is to cook food slowly in a little liquid in a closed pot.

clue.text: Terriers, maybe male ones with tail spinning

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for male

indicators.note: spinning things whirl round and land in a different order, so these letters are mixed

parts.note: one is I in Roman numerals, so two of them
anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Male terrier dogs chase their own tails, spinning round and round.
explanation.walkthrough: Terriers is old British slang for the Territorial Army, Britain's part-time volunteer reserve, not the dogs.
explanation.definitionFit: The Territorial Army is a body of part-time citizen soldiers, which is what a militia is.

clue.text: Synthetic cheese rolls on hand

parts.note: a hand is a worker, a man

indicators.note: a thing that rolls over is turned the other way, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: Edam is a Dutch cheese

explanation.surface: Fake cheese is on sale in rolls, ready to hand.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue, 'on' puts the cheese after the worker.
explanation.definitionFit: Man-made materials are artificial ones produced by people rather than occurring naturally, the sense of synthetic.

clue.text: Bond welcoming kiss over death

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means turned upside down, so it reads from bottom to top
welcoming someone takes them in, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: a tie is a bond
X is the kiss at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: James Bond kisses a woman over the dead body of his enemy.
explanation.walkthrough: Bond tempts us towards 007; it is just a link or tie.
explanation.definitionFit: An exit is a departure, and death is often called one's final exit from life's stage.

clue.text: Cheers engulfing massed partygoers either side of level crossing

indicators.note: engulfing means swallowing whole, so one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: ta is British informal thanks, like cheers
ravers are people at raves, big dance parties

indicators.note: either side means one of the outside letters of the word that follows

parts.note: both its ends are the same letter, so either side gives it

explanation.surface: Cheering crowds of revellers surround the level crossing on a railway.
explanation.walkthrough: Level crossing looks like one phrase; crossing alone is the definition. Ta is British slang for thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: A traversal is the act of travelling across something, which is a crossing.

clue.text: Food from America kept in vessel that doesn't close

indicators.note: something that does not close lacks its ending, so the final letter is dropped
kept in means held inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a ship is a vessel, here without its last letter
US is short for America

explanation.surface: American food is kept aboard a ship whose doors won't shut.
explanation.definitionFit: Sushi is a Japanese dish of vinegared rice with raw fish, a kind of food.
